eventMetadata.context_description: San Francisco's late-summer temperatures hinge on the depth and persistence of the marine layer—the cool, moist air mass advected onshore by prevailing northwest winds. A modestly compressed layer (around 1,000 feet recently) permits greater afternoon heating under subsidence from high pressure, supporting highs near 70–71 °F, while a deeper layer sustains fog and stratus that reflect sunlight and cap readings at 68–69 °F. Current model consensus shows a stable pattern with no major trough or ridge shift through August 20, keeping conditions close to the long-term August mean of 67 °F at the airport. Minor day-to-day variations in onshore flow strength and cloud cover will decide whether the market’s two leading brackets resolve higher or lower, with NWS guidance currently tilting toward the upper end of that range.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent southwest monsoon (habagat) activity over Luzon is the dominant influence on Manila temperatures heading into August 21, driving cloudy skies, scattered showers, and thunderstorms that limit daytime heating. PAGASA outlooks indicate highs near 29–32 °C with 40–70 % rain chances, consistent with seasonal norms for the period when monsoon moisture and cloud cover typically suppress peaks below the 33–34 °C range seen in drier months. No tropical cyclones or strong high-pressure systems are expected to alter this pattern through the weekend, keeping conditions stable. Official resolution will rely on PAGASA station readings for the daily maximum, with any last-minute forecast shifts in monsoon strength or timing serving as the main variable for traders monitoring updated model guidance.
